## Presentation shortcuts

Slides are currently available for the chapter key and chapters 1–10.
You can view them by clicking the screen icon <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
  viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="1.1em" height="1.1em"
  style="vertical-align: -0.15em"
  fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6"
  stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"
  aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
  <rect x="3" y="3" width="18" height="13" rx="1"/>
  <path d="M12 16v5m-4 0h8m-9-10 3-4 3 2 3-3"/>
</svg> beside a chapter title.

::: {.slide-bullet}

1. Press `?` to explore the keyboard shortcuts.
2. Close the shortcut help with `Esc` or `Q`, then press `E` to enter PDF-export mode.
3. Open your browser's print dialog and choose **Save as PDF**. Press `E` again to return to the slides.

:::

## Learning outcomes & summaries

::: {.callout-note title="Learning outcomes & Chapter summary" collapse=false}
[Every chapter starts with the "Learning outcomes"]{.slide-bullet},
which describe what you will learn from this chapter.
To make these learning outcomes more useful to you as a reader,
we have expanded them to include a summary of the "solution" for each outcome,
instead of just stating what you are to learn in the chapter.

For example,
instead of simply stating:
"Explain the main advantage of visualizing data"
we would write:
"Explain that the main advantage of visualizing data
instead of presenting it with numbers is that they are easier to interpret for humans.

As such,
[the learning objectives also serve as the summary of each chapter]{.slide-bullet}.
:::

## Coding content

[Coding content will often include a panel with multiple tabs]{.slide-bullet},
so that you can easily see what the same code looks like
for different visualization packages.
These sections also include explanations
that are specific to the code of a certain package,
rather than being about data visualization in general.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Package One {.slide-fragment .slide-with-content}

```{python}
#| label: package-example-python
#| slide-show: both
#| slide-output-fragment: true
# Code for the first package, e.g.:
range(5)

```

#| label: package-example-r

::: {.column-margin}

**Margin content**

Content in the margin usually
includes
figure legends,
factual tidbits,
historical explanations,
etymology,
and more.

:::

::: {.deep-dive}

Deep dives
include content that
is not essential to understand main topics of the chapter.
Instead,
these sections elaborate on concepts
and often contains more challenging content.

:::
